patch.value: The edge-count floor is denominated over a population that includes the edges the graph itself calls redundant, so repairing 73 witnessed implied ordering rows and silently relaxing the guard are the same privileged act

pm graph redundancy computes 73 transitively implied ordering edges (35 blocks + 38 blocked_by), each carrying a witness path, so the product already names them as adding no ordering information. graph-profile-edges-floor is denominated in TOTAL deduplicated directed edges and stands at 11871 against 11875 observed, so the gate-admissible repair is at most 4 of 73 (5.5%). Beyond that the run reports floor_undercut, and --update resolves floors with Math.max, so the gate cannot absorb the reduction either. The declaration's own note anticipates this and prescribes a hand edit of the number. That is the defect: in the resulting diff, repairing a witnessed defect population and silently relaxing a quality floor are byte-indistinguishable acts, both requiring the same privileged edit, so the guard cannot tell a cleanup from an erosion. Denominating the floor over informative edges (total minus redundant) makes the two motions distinguishable without any privileged act: removing an implied edge drops both terms and is neutral, while removing a load-bearing edge still breaches. Dual of pm-c90tfh, which owns the ADDITION direction (the blocks ceiling sits at 243 with zero headroom, so ordering edges cannot be added either); together the two mean the ordering relation is frozen in both directions while three open items require changing it.

The measurement ratchet exposes a graph_analytic selector source so a declaration can be denominated over a population the graph analytics compute rather than only over the audit census; A floor exists over informative edges (total deduplicated directed edges minus the redundancy analytic's redundant_count) so that removing a witnessed implied edge is bound-neutral and removing a load-bearing edge still breaches; redundant_count carries a ceiling so the witnessed implied-ordering population can only shrink, and a run that grows it fails; The total-edge floor is retired in the same change that lands its replacement, with the re-denomination recorded in the declaration note rather than left as an unexplained lowered number; A negative control proves both directions: removing a redundant edge passes and removing an informative edge fails

graph-profile-edges-floor floor=11871 observed=11875 (headroom 4); pm graph redundancy redundant_count=73; removing 5+ redundant edges fails the release gate with floor_undercut; scripts/release/tracker-measurement-gate.mjs resolves floors with Math.max(declaration.floor, entry.observed) so --update never lowers one

patch.value: The floor is re-denominated over a derived measurement (total deduplicated directed edges minus the redundancy analytic's implied ordering rows) declared as pm data, not as a patch to a gate script; redundant_count carries a declared ceiling so the witnessed implied-ordering population can only shrink; Removing a witnessed implied edge is bound-neutral and removing a load-bearing edge still breaches, proven by a negative control in both directions; Lowering any floor requires a linked Decision item, so a repair and an erosion are no longer the same hand edit of a number

message: Re-point the fix at native SDK primitives: denomination belongs in a derived measurement, not in a gate script
